Mission Local reported that Alemany Farm, San Francisco’s largest urban farm, was at risk of shutting down after one-time city funding ran out, leaving a projected $100,000–$150,000 budget gap. The farm had paused paid apprenticeships, reduced staff hours and launched a $200,000 fundraising campaign to stay afloat.

“After years of relying on thin public grants and volunteer labor, the farm paused its paid apprenticeship programs at the start of May, scaled back staff hours near the same time, and launched a grassroots campaign to raise $200,000 in late April, an effort to stay afloat in a city cutting costs across public services”

“The urban farm, structured as a fiscally sponsored nonprofit, is facing a $100,000 to $150,000 gap in this year’s budget after one-time city funding ran out, according to farm organizers.”

Correction: A previous version of this story attributed the farm’s projected budget gap to the San Francisco Human Services Agency. The estimate came from Alemany Farm.
